title: Attention kernel arbiter with confidence-based fallback for v2/v3
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a runtime kernel arbiter that picks between FlashAttention v2 and v3 (and safe fallbacks) per-request using a lightweight confidence estimator and runtime shape/latency signals. Goal: reduce regressions where v3 increases decode latency or introduces instability for specific short/edge-case request shapes while preserving v3 cost/latency benefits for compatible workloads.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New arbiter routes >=95% of short-context requests to the selected stable kernel profile without increasing 95th percentile latency beyond baseline for the rollout cohort. 2) Fallback triggers for requests with high token-entropy/attention-variance and recovers within one request without user-visible errors. 3) Telemetry adds per-request decision_reason tag and confidence score; dashboards show decision distribution by model, sequence_length, and tenant. 4) End-to-end A/B rollout plan + canary with automatic rollback on SLO regressions.
reproduction_steps: 1) Run synthetic microbenchmarks with sequence lengths {8,16,32,64} and head_count variations using production-like batch mixing. 2) Replay sampled production traces where we observed v3 regressions (linked). 3) Run long-duration burst tests with KV cache warm/cold cycles. 4) Enable v3 kernel by default and track per-request fallback counts.
investigation_notes:
- Observed pattern: regressions concentrated on short sequences (<=16) and heterogeneous microbatching with mixed qkv layout; v3 kernel warmup plus microtiling mismatch increases latency in ~0.6% of requests.
- Telemetry shows spikes in per-head attention variance correlating with decode jitter.
- Prefill + decode interleaving can cause v3 kernel to allocate transient workspace more frequently, causing small GC-like stalls on some drivers.
- Existing heuristic selectors are static (batch-size, seq-len) and do not consider runtime confidence or recent kernel success history.
proposed_solution: 1) Build 'Kernel Arbiter' component that: a) computes a lightweight confidence_score for the request using fast probes (first N tokens logits entropy and attention variance statistics from prefill), b) consults a per-model kernel policy table (preferred kernel, hysteresis thresholds), and c) selects kernel variant. 2) Implement a soft-fallback mechanism: if confidence_score below threshold or if kernel reports workspace/launch errors/latency spike, switch to fallback kernel for remaining decode tokens with no request failure. 3) Add short-term request-level memoization: if a tenant's recent requests hit fallback > X% in last Y minutes, bias arbiter to safe kernel for that tenant until metric cools. 4) Expose decision_reason and confidence_score in trace metadata for postmortem and rollout metrics.
work_items: Design kernel arbiter API and policy schema (runtime + control-plane integration)
Implement confidence estimator (probe size N configurable), integrate with prefill path
Implement soft-fallback handshake between kernels preserving KV cache and hidden-state continuity
Add per-tenant short-term memoization store + eviction policy
Instrument telemetry tags: decision_reason, confidence_score, fallback_reason, kernel_latency_delta
Create rollouts: canary cohorts, automatic SLO checks and rollback hooks
End-to-end tests: synthetic microbenchmarks + production trace replay
Run 2-week shadow run and then a staged canary rollout
risks:
- Increased decision path CPU overhead; must be <0.5ms median to avoid negating latency wins.
- Incorrect confidence heuristics could bias away from v3 gains.
- Memoization may mask transient bugs and delay root cause detection.
- Complexity in preserving KV cache/decoder state across kernel switches; potential for correctness bugs if handshake incomplete.
metrics_to_track: 95th and 99th percentile decode latency (canary vs baseline)
cost-per-token delta for requests routed to v3
